items.title: Farbrace leaves Sussex to join Lancashire
items.description: Lancashire appoint Paul Farbrace as their new director of cricket weeks before he was due to begin the same role at Sussex.

items.title: ECB may fund women's Windies Test to aid Ashes preparation
items.description: The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) will “look at” the unusual step of funding a women’s Test in the West Indies next year in order to aid England’s Ashes preparations.

items.title: India v West Indies - first T20 scorecard
items.description: Latest scorecard from the first Twenty20 international between India and West Indies in Lucknow.

items.title: Australia warm-up shows England have 'learned' from Ashes
items.description: England confirm warm-up fixture at the Waca before this winter's white-ball tour of Australia - a stark contrast to last year's Ashes defeat.

items.title: India's Harmanpreet steps down as captain
items.description: India batter Harmanpreet Kaur leaves her role as national team captain across all three formats of international cricket.

items.title: India beat Pakistan to take Asian Games gold
items.description: Abhishek Sharma and Tilak Varma set India on their way to victory as they beat Pakistan to win gold at the Asian Games.

items.title: Pretorius breaks Gayle's T20 record score
items.description: Lhuan-dre Pretorius breaks Chris Gayle's record for the highest score in a men's T20 match with an unbeaten 188 in a domestic fixture in South Africa.

items.title: Carse charged but remains available for England
items.description: Brydon Carse is charged by the Cricket Regulator over an incident outside a Derby nightclub but remains available for selection by England.

items.title: Bowler Miles retires to protect 'mental well-being'
items.description: Gloucestershire bowler Craig Miles retires from professional cricket to protect his "mental well-being".

items.title: Sussex sign seamer Dudgeon on two-year deal
items.description: Sussex sign South African seamer Keith Dudgeon, who helped Kent win County Championship promotion in 2026, on a two-year contract.

items.title: Harmison signs first professional Durham deal
items.description: Charlie Harmison, son of 2005 Ashes winner Steve, signs a two-year deal with Durham.

items.title: England call up Crane and rest Archer for Pakistan series
items.description: Leg-spinner Mason Crane has the chance to play for England for the first time in eight years after being recalled for the one-day international tri-series in Pakistan.

items.title: Stumped
items.description: Players face pay cuts and tournaments have been suspended

items.title: Kent trigger Milnes and Northeast extensions
items.description: Kent trigger contract extension clauses for seamer Matt Milnes and experienced batter Sam Northeast.

items.title: Australia call up Maddinson after cancer recovery
items.description: Australia recall Nic Maddinson for the first Test against South Africa after the New South Wales batter recovered from testicular cancer.

items.title: Overton hopes to make England selectors' job hard
items.description: Somerset all-rounder Craig Overton says he wants to make England selectors' jobs "as hard as possible" by continuing to play well.

items.title: England avoid Australia & India in World Cup draw
items.description: England avoid defending champions Australia and world number one-ranked side India in the group-stage draw for the 2027 ICC Cricket World Cup.

items.title: Australian Hughes among five leaving Sussex
